# unresolved-guarded-read (MUT206)

Family: Mutation & State (MUT) · Heuristic · Runs when its contract is declared · Severity `error` (a bug) · No automatic fix

Strict mode of a `read-owners` contract (`unresolved = "report"`): reading an attribute named like a target on an object of unknown class.

!!! note "Heuristic"

    This rule is heuristic: a premise of its claim can be open ("What a report states" lists them), so a report can be wrong about the code. It runs when its contract is declared. It has not been measured yet. See [Rule Precision](../precision.md).

## What it does
The strict mode of a `[[tool.heki.read-owners]]` contract that sets `unresolved = "report"`:
reports the reads outside the read owners that `MUT203` cannot tie to a target class, so a clean
`MUT203` run says how much it did not check. A read of an attribute named like a target attribute
(`children` for `Reference.children`; for `Reference.*`, a name `Reference`, a project subclass,
or a project base gives its instances in project code, not one only a base outside the project
gives them, [configuration](../configuration.md#globs-on-objects-of-unknown-class)) is reported
once, at the read,
when its object is of unknown class: an unannotated parameter, a loop variable, the result of a
call heki does not resolve, a value annotated `Any` or `object` (unless an `isinstance` test
around the read narrows it to a class), a protocol whose implementations heki cannot list (one
without members, or implemented by more than eight classes), or a variable of an enclosing
function that a nested scope rebinds (`nonlocal`). `obj.children`, a local alias of it,
`getattr(obj, "children")` and `hasattr(obj, "children")` with a constant name, and `obj.__dict__["children"]` (also
`vars(obj)["children"]`) count, as for `MUT203`.

The rules of `MUT203` for what is allowed apply: allowed readers, exempt methods, functions that
only run inside allowed readers, `forbidden-readers` (the reading function must be one), and
`allowed-protocols`, also for an object heki cannot tie to a class that is typed with a named
protocol declaring the attribute: a class object typed `type[P]` (a parameter, a local, or an
attribute annotated so), or an instance of a protocol whose implementations heki cannot list.
`MUT203` does not follow a read into a parameter that its function does not type, so the callers
decide for such a parameter: the read is reported unless every caller path binds an instance of
a project class outside the targets' classes to it. A parameter some caller binds to an instance
of a target class is reported here: that read is a read of the target that no other rule sees.
With `attribution = "lexical"`, a function that only runs inside allowed readers is not allowed,
and a caller path through an allowed reader counts like any other: the read is the function's
own, and its callers only tell the object's class.

The help names up to three allowed readers that read a target of the attribute's name
themselves, as for `MUT203`, after the contract's `message`:
``allowed readers of `children`: ...``.

## What a report states

A report states that, outside the read owners, the function reads an attribute named like a target
of the `read-owners` contract on an object whose class heki does not know.

Its premises:

- **Named like a target**: the attribute's name matches a target's. Established.
- **Unknown class**: heki did not resolve the class of the object. Established: the claim is about
  heki's own resolution.
- **Outside the owners**: the function is not in the allowed modules and classes, nor runs only
  inside allowed contexts (with `attribution = "lexical"`: the function holding the access is not
  allowed). Established from the contract.

## Why is this bad?
`MUT203` reports what it can back with a class: a read through an object it cannot type is not
followed, so a contract that passes says nothing about those reads. Name-based checkers report
them all; heki reports them separately, under their own code, so they can be counted, ratcheted
with a baseline, and reduced by annotating the objects, without mixing them with the violations
`MUT203` proves.

## Example
```toml
[[tool.heki.read-owners]]
name = "reference-children"
targets = ["Reference.children"]
allowed-readers = ["*GenerationIndex*"]
unresolved = "report"
```

```python
def render(ref) -> str:  # no annotation: heki cannot tell what `ref` is
    return ", ".join(map(str, ref.children))  # MUT206


def size(ref: Reference) -> int:
    return len(ref.children)  # MUT203: a typed read
```

Use instead:
```python
def render(ref: Reference, index: GenerationIndex) -> str:
    return ", ".join(map(str, index.children_of(ref)))
```

## Fix safety
No automatic fix.

## Options
- `[[tool.heki.read-owners]]`:
  - `unresolved`: `"ignore"` (default) or `"report"`.
  - `targets`, `allowed-readers`, `forbidden-readers`, `exempt-methods`, `attribution`,
    `message`: as for `MUT203`.
